title: Bounded strict filtered-colimit closure after qcqs direct image
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring, with pulled-back internal module categories $\mathcal A_U,\mathcal A_V$ and actual ordinary derived direct image $Rb_*$ [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. Let $b:U\to V$ be weakly etale, quasi-compact and quasi-separated between quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, sk-def-pe-morphisms, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Let $P$ be an object property of $D(\mathcal A_V)$ satisfying $\operatorname{IsSupportedModelHullClass}(\Lambda,V,P)$ [def-sfb-supported-model-hull]. Let $I$ be a small filtered category in the fixed indexing universe, $D:I\to\operatorname{CochainComplex}(\mathcal A_U,\mathbf Z)$ a strict diagram and $a\in\mathbf Z$ such that $D_i^n$ is zero for every $i$ and $n<a$ [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-category-colimit, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Suppose $P(Rb_*QD_i)$ for every $i$. Then for every colimit cocone $c$ of $D$, $P(Rb_*Q(c.\mathrm{pt}))$. Here $Q$ is the ordinary localization of complexes at quasi-isomorphisms and $c$ is a colimit before localization, computed termwise. This is only preservation of the strict common-bound filtered-colimit closure clause for the inverse-image class; it does not assert preservation of any supported generator or descend hull membership. No admissibility condition is required on $\Lambda$. Zero diagrams and all integer lower bounds are allowed.

proof.text: Transport the internal module direct image and strict diagram to section-ring modules using the exact internal/section-module equivalences. These equivalences preserve the actual direct-image adjunction and colimits.

Let $C_i$ be a strict diagram indexed by a small filtered category $I$, zero below $a$. Regard it as one bounded-below complex in $\operatorname{Fun}(I,\operatorname{Mod}(\Lambda_U))$. This category is Grothendieck and has enough injectives. Apply the all-lower-bounds Cartan--Eilenberg existence theorem and its total-resolution theorem there to obtain a strict quasi-isomorphism $C\to H$; its total is still zero below $a$ and has injective terms, since each diagonal is a finite sum of injectives. Evaluation at $i$ preserves injectives: its left adjoint sends $M$ at $j$ to $\bigoplus_{\operatorname{Hom}_I(i,j)}M$ and is exact. Indeed that sum is the filtered colimit of its finite subsums, and finite sums and filtered colimits are exact in a Grothendieck category. The extension property for an evaluated injective now follows by adjunction from this exact left adjoint. Hence $C_i\to H_i$ are bounded-below injective resolutions with the same bound and strictly compatible arrows; each $H_i$, being bounded below with injective terms, is K-injective by the bounded-below injective criterion. Consequently $b_*H_i$ are strict representatives, zero below $a$, of $Rb_*QC_i$.

proof.text: The strict diagram $b_*H_i$ in the preceding step has the same common lower bound and represents $Rb_*QD_i$. Use repleteness to put its terms in $P$ and apply the strict filtered-colimit clause of $P$. The canonical comparison $Q\varinjlim b_*H_i\to Rb_*Q\varinjlim H_i$ is an isomorphism on every cohomology sheaf by bounded continuity; hence it is an isomorphism. Exact filtered colimits make $\varinjlim D_i\to\varinjlim H_i$ a quasi-isomorphism. Transport membership through both isomorphisms, the module equivalences, and the unique isomorphism between colimit cocones. This proves the conclusion for the given $c$.
